title: EIF framework lock (.eif/framework.lock.yaml) - EIF-managed, never hand-edited
description: Exact provenance of the materialized instance runtime: which framework commit, whether the source was dirty, the exact bundle file hashes, which adapter entrypoint was generated, and when. Fully regenerated by scripts/eif_init.py on every init/upgrade - a routine upgrade rewrites this file completely and never touches the user-owned .eif/config.yaml. See docs/architecture/instance-contract.md.

ref.description: Real framework git commit this instance was generated from - always a full 40-hex SHA, never a placeholder or branch name.

dirty.description: True if --framework-root's working tree had uncommitted changes when this bundle was materialized - the actual detected state, independent of ref_verification. See --allow-dirty in eif_init.py.

ref_verification.description: git-verified: ref came from `git rev-parse HEAD` on --framework-root. asserted: ref was supplied via --framework-ref (e.g. framework-root is not a git checkout) - trustworthy only as far as whoever passed that flag. Distinguishing the two prevents an asserted ref from silently reading as git-verified provenance.

manifest.description: Every file eif_init.py's BUNDLE_SCRIPTS/BUNDLE_TREES copied FROM THE FRAMEWORK SOURCE, hashed before copying. Scope is precise, not 'everything under the bundle path': files written into the bundle AFTER staging (README.md) and interpreter-generated files (__pycache__/) are intentionally outside this list - see eif_verify_runtime.py's KNOWN_UNMANIFESTED_* classification, which reports any OTHER unlisted file as a real integrity concern rather than ignoring it.

digest.description: Combined hash over the sorted manifest - lets a consumer verify the whole bundle in one comparison without re-hashing every file.

knowledge_index.description: Provenance of the EIF-managed knowledge index, present only when eif_init.py actually created or regenerated one this run (knowledge.managed: true and a knowledge root exists) - absent entirely when the index was skipped. Lets eif_verify_runtime.py detect drift: a hand-edited index file (hash mismatch) or one that has silently lost its ownership marker.

package.description: Present only when this instance was generated by the installed eifctl package (engineering_intelligence_framework) rather than a framework git checkout. framework.ref/ref_verification are still populated in this case (ref_verification: asserted, ref set to a package-derived synthetic value) since they're required - this section carries the genuinely additional provenance a package install has that a checkout doesn't: which distribution, which release, which interpreter.

distribution.description: The installed package's distribution name (importlib.metadata terms), e.g. 'engineering-intelligence-framework'.

version.description: The installed package's own version (importlib.metadata.version) - independent of framework.ref, which for a package source is asserted/synthetic rather than a real git commit.

python_version.description: 'major.minor.micro' of the interpreter that ran `eifctl init`.
